findings.location: src/Benchmarks.Harness/nativeweave_bench.py: RunState.event, read_events and run_plan failure handling
findings.requirement: A21 integrity/counter validation and D13 section7 preserve failure datasets and traces.
findings.observed: A target JSON array [] raises AttributeError because event.get is called without object validation. The reader does not catch this exception; run_cell exits without writing result.json and run_plan does not catch AttributeError. The independent fixture reproduced output_preserved=false.
findings.requested: Validate event and counter object shape before access; preserve the invalid raw event, known rows and last counters as an invalid cell without discarding the run.
findings.resolution: Event and counter object shapes are validated before field access. The independent same [] mutation now produces an invalid cell with both request rows and an exact-byte, hashed raw event JSONL file, instead of raising AttributeError and losing the cell.

findings.requirement: A21 step4 and D13 section5 retain managed/native allocation, copy, owner and resource observations and raw samples.
findings.observed: Completion counters are validated then overwritten in last_target_counters; neither normal request rows nor raw event history retains them. Distinct measured allocation observations1 and2 leave only2, so per-operation costs cannot be reconstructed.
findings.requested: Retain each completion observation or an equivalent lossless raw event dataset with observer timestamps, including failures and late events.
findings.resolution: Each completion now stores target_counters and target_completion_observed_ns on its request row, with exact raw line persistence before parsing. Independent varied values1 and2 survive in both rows and raw completions. All600 final normal-run counter rows match the1200 raw admission/completion lines.

findings.requirement: D13 section3 offered/admitted/completed throughput must use consistent timestamps and retain timeouts.
findings.observed: A completion observed81.130598ms after scheduled arrival, after a20ms timeout, is counted in completed but divided by the effective20ms timeout window. The cell reports50/s although the matching observed endpoint implies12.325806/s. The timeout classification is correctly retained; the throughput denominator is wrong.
findings.requested: Use an observed measurement endpoint consistent with counted admission/completion events or explicitly separate in-window and late counts. Keep effective deadline and actual observation time distinct.
findings.resolution: Effective deadline, timeout observation and target completion observation are separate. The rate observation window extends through counted late events. The independent delayed response remains a timeout and now reports12.24359164291614/s over81.67538ms, with an exactly consistent numerator/denominator.

findings.requirement: D01 sections1/4 and D13 section2 require exact compiler/linker identities.
findings.observed: The recorded linker is GCC14, which is the explicitly selected driver. AOT logs show -fuse-ld=bfd but no ld binary version/hash is recorded; Rust link args are absent.
findings.requested: Record Rust actual emitted link arguments and selected linker path/hash/version, and distinguish GCC driver from GNU BFD linker for AOT.
findings.resolution: Verification explicitly selects GCC/BFD, records actual Rust emitted link arguments and Native AOT publish arguments, and separately records GCC14 driver and GNU ld2.44 paths, hashes and versions. Both binary hashes and all four actual link commands were independently checked.

review_conclusions: Scheduled arrivals, dispatch, observed admission, timeout/completion and generator lag are separate under one observer monotonic clock. Dispatch never waits for a response; backpressure and missed/capacity/lag limits invalidate the intended offered-rate cell.

The finite omission accounting counterexample and rejection of expected-interval correction satisfy the no-double-correction boundary. All outcome rows, raw histogram bins, exact percentiles, overflow and invalid cells remain available.

The four original findings were real narrow accounting/provenance defects, were fixed in the reviewed commit, and passed the same independent reproductions. Exact malformed bytes and per-operation counter observations now survive; throughput uses an observation window consistent with counted late completions.

Counter units, availability and methods are explicit. Unavailable counters remain unknown/null, not zero. Procfs/GC measurements declare their actual scope; no queue/credit limit is described as a whole-memory cap. Process exit/kill is expressly not retirement proof.

The final author run has24 successful commands, real JIT and Native AOT executions, direct Rust execution,19 focused regressions, six independent process cells and600 requests. The reviewer checked all14 source files against committed bytes,50 artifacts,34 locked Design inputs, driver/linker hashes and1200 raw event lines without redundantly rebuilding the full pipeline.

There are no public application types in either compiled fixture assembly and no benchmark dependency enters a product package. The guide covers setup, immutable plans, oracle input, errors, cancellation/cleanup limits, counter interpretation and advanced operation.

No actual Database/ORM/Server superiority, production memory benefit, all-platform completion or final pristine-package acceptance is asserted. The scalar three-route sample validates the controller and adapter path only; B23/B22/A16/B24 retain their designated work.
